record.paper_title: Exact results and open questions in first principle functional RG
record.original_question: Can the direct finite-temperature loop expansion of the functional renormalization group be reorganized or resummed in a consistent way, equivalent to the exact renormalization-group treatment, so that it remains quantitatively valid beyond the low-loop regime instead of failing in the thermal boundary layer?

evidence.quote: However, we cannot exclude that a clever way may exist to resum consistently, equivalent to what is done with the ERG.

artifact.category_tag: functional renormalization group at finite temperature
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a disordered elastic system (such as a random-field or random-manifold model) whose effective action at temperature $T>0$ is studied via the functional renormalization group (FRG) for the renormalized disorder correlator $R(u)$ (or its second derivative $\Delta(u) = -R''(u)$). At zero temperature, $\Delta(u)$ develops a non-analytic cusp at $u=0$; at finite temperature $T>0$, the cusp is rounded into a thermal boundary layer of width proportional to $T$, inside which $\Delta(u)$ is smooth.

The direct finite-$T$ loop expansion of the FRG flow equations for $R(u)$ is organized as a perturbative series in the number of loops, with vertices given by the bare disorder correlator and its derivatives. Inside the thermal boundary layer, the higher-loop contributions to $\Delta(u)$ at scale $\ell$ are enhanced by inverse powers of $T$ (and of the boundary-layer width), so that successive terms of the loop expansion become of the same order: the naive loop expansion ceases to be quantitatively reliable in the boundary-layer region, even though the exact renormalization group (ERG) treatment of the same flow yields a finite, well-defined result there.

Problem. Does there exist a systematic reorganization or resummation of the direct finite-temperature loop expansion of the FRG — for instance, a partial summation of an infinite class of diagrams, a change of variables/expansion parameter, or an ansatz capturing the boundary-layer scaling — that:

(i) reproduces, order by order in the reorganized series, the boundary-layer behaviour of $\Delta(u)$ obtained from the exact renormalization group;

(ii) remains quantitatively valid beyond the low-loop regime, throughout the thermal boundary layer of width $\sim T$ around $u=0$; and

(iii) reduces, in the regime where the standard loop expansion is controlled (away from the boundary layer), to that standard expansion?

Either construct such a resummation explicitly and prove its equivalence to the ERG result in the boundary layer, or prove that no such consistent resummation of the direct finite-$T$ loop expansion exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the direct finite-temperature loop expansion of the functional RG for disordered elastic systems can be consistently resummed to match the exact RG treatment in the thermal boundary layer was raised as an open problem and no published resolution has been located. Subsequent FRG literature on disordered systems continues to rely on the exact/Wetterich RG to access the boundary layer, suggesting the issue remains open.

status_evidence.claim: The possibility of a consistent resummation of the direct finite-T loop expansion is left open.
